meta.name: Score ATS candidates and enroll top matches into Supabase outreach campaigns

name: Score ATS candidates into a Supabase outreach campaign

nodes.name: Job order created
nodes.notes: Point the ATS webhook subscription here. Bullhorn: Events API. CEIPAL / Recruit CRM: their outbound webhook settings.

nodes.name: [cred] AI - read the job description
nodes.notes: Runs ONCE PER JOB ORDER, not per candidate — a few hundred tokens per campaign. It fills in blanks; it never decides who is contacted. Blank AI_API_KEY skips it entirely and the keyword rules stand alone.

nodes.name: [cred] ATS - search candidates
nodes.notes: THE one node that changes per ATS vendor. Everything downstream reads the normalised shape, so swapping Bullhorn for CEIPAL is this node and the ATS_FIELDS map in config.

nodes.name: [cred] Supabase - engagement history
nodes.notes: One call, not three. A half-populated suppression list is worse than none, so opt-outs, recent touches and live enrollments come back together or not at all.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_client_id: $('config').first().json.client_id, p_ats_job_id: $('the job spec').first().json.ats_job_id, p_phones: $('score against the job order').all().map(i => i.json.phone_e164).filter(Boolean) }) }}

nodes.name: [cred] Supabase - upsert the campaign
nodes.notes: The unique index on (client_id, idempotency_key) is what makes an ATS webhook delivered three times create one campaign.

nodes.name: [cred] Supabase - insert the enrollments
nodes.notes: ignore-duplicates, not merge. Re-running a launch must never reset somebody's step counter back to zero and text them again.

parameters.content:
## Score ATS candidates into a Supabase outreach campaign

**Who's it for**
Recruitment agencies and in-house talent teams who already keep candidates in an ATS and want a
scored, compliant shortlist enrolled into outreach automatically, instead of a recruiter picking
names by hand.

**How it works**
A new job order arrives by webhook, or you press **Run it now**. The job is normalised through a
per-vendor field map, then optionally enriched by an AI call that pulls out the must-have and
nice-to-have requirements. Candidates are fetched from the ATS, normalised (phone numbers to E.164,
duplicates collapsed) and scored against the job order transparently. Engagement history is read
from Supabase so the gate can reject opt-outs, anyone inside a cooldown window, anyone already in
another live campaign, everyone below the score floor, and anything over the per-run cap. Survivors
are enrolled with a first touch *scheduled* — never sent. Workflow 2 owns every outbound message,
which keeps quiet hours and the daily cap in one place.

**How to set up**
1. Open **`config`** and set `ATS_FIELDS` for your vendor, the score floor and the per-run cap.
2. Attach your credentials to the four `[cred]` nodes.
3. Leave **`DEMO_MODE = true`** for the first run — it uses the sample pool and writes nothing.

**Requirements**
An ATS with a candidate search API, a Supabase project, and optionally an OpenAI-compatible
endpoint and a Slack or Discord webhook.

**How to customize**
Scoring weights, the cooldown window and the gate thresholds all live in `config`. To add a
sourcing channel, feed it into **`one candidate pool`** and the rest of the pipeline is unchanged.

### 1. Read the job order

The ATS posts a new job order to **`Job order created`**, or you press **`Run it now`** to use the sample.

**`config`** holds every setting in one place. **`read the job order`** maps the vendor payload through `ATS_FIELDS`, so a new ATS is one map entry, not a new workflow.

**`job order usable?`** rejects a job with no title or no requirements before anything is spent on it.

### 2. Enrich the spec (optional)

**`AI worth calling?`** only spends a token when the job order is thin. A well-filled order skips straight to the keyword rules.

**`apply the AI requirements`** merges the extracted must-haves and nice-to-haves over the parsed order — the AI adds to the spec, it never replaces what the ATS already told us.

### 3. Source and score the candidates

**`[cred] ATS - search candidates`** runs the search; with no ATS credential the run falls back to the bundled sample pool, so you can see the whole pipeline before connecting anything.

**`normalise the candidates`** puts phone numbers in E.164 and collapses duplicates. **`score against the job order`** scores every candidate transparently — the reason is carried next to the score.

### 4. The gate

Nobody is enrolled who does not pass every check, and every rejection is kept with the reason next to the name — so *"why was this person not contacted"* is as answerable as *"why were they"*.

The order is deliberate. **Opt-out is checked before the score**, because an opted-out number is never reconsidered on the grounds that the job is a good fit.

### 5. Enrol the survivors

The job order, campaign and candidates are upserted first, then **`link the enrollments`** resolves the returned ids so an enrollment can never point at a row that does not exist.

Each enrollment is written with its first touch **scheduled**, not sent.

nodes.name: 6. Nothing is written until you say so

parameters.content:
### 6. Nothing is written until you say so

`DEMO_MODE = true` (how it ships) runs the whole pipeline against the sample pool and writes nothing. Open **`STOP: preview - nothing enrolled`** to read the entire launch: who would be enrolled, in what order, with what score, and everyone held back and why.

Set `DEMO_MODE = false` and fill in Supabase to persist a campaign. Even then **no message is sent** — that is workflow 2, and it has its own gate.
